queue.title: Bound the fastmcp dependency before CI resolves into FastMCP 4 and goes red
queue.detail:
FOUND BY TONIGHT'S RESEARCH RUN, and it is the most urgent thing in this queue because it can turn CI red on the next push without anyone touching the code. Read spec-queue/research/2026-09-01.md section '### 1.' for the full evidence.
FACTS IT MEASURED: FastMCP 4.0.0 published to PyPI 2026-08-31T18:20:31Z. This repo declares `fastmcp>=2.0` UNBOUNDED in pyproject.toml:39 and :60 and hub/pyproject.toml:19. CI resolves fresh with no lockfile (.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-36). It installed 4.0.0 in a scratch venv and probed the four APIs hub/hub/mcp_server.py actually uses: all four survive and Literal enums still render -- BUT `FastMCP.get_tools()` is GONE, and that is the introspection layer seven test files sit on. The operator's machine still has 3.4.5, so local green proves nothing about CI.
VERIFY BEFORE ACTING -- the research is a lead, not a verdict. Confirm the pin strings at those exact lines, confirm which tests import or call get_tools(), and confirm 4.0.0 is what a fresh resolve picks today. If any of that does not hold, say so in the log and drop the item rather than 'fixing' something that is not broken.
IF IT HOLDS: apply a defensive UPPER BOUND (e.g. `fastmcp>=2.0,<4`) in all three places. Do not downgrade anything, do not add a lockfile, and do not touch any OTHER unbounded dependency -- `fastapi>=0.110` is an open operator decision (it is in decisions_for_user) and is NOT yours tonight. Add a test that fails when the tool surface's actual APIs stop resolving, so the next major is caught by a named test rather than by CI going red. Run the tool-surface parity tests and `pytest hub/tests/` in the chunk that covers mcp_server.
Then ADD to decisions_for_user: 'fastmcp was bounded to <4 on 2026-09-01 defensively; ratify or widen', with the measured evidence. A bound is reversible in one line, which is why taking it unattended is defensible where changing fastapi would not be.
queue.outcome: DONE, iteration 1, 2026-09-01T01:26+01:00. fastmcp>=2.0 -> fastmcp>=2.0,<4 in all three declarations, plus hub/tests/test_fastmcp_api_contract.py (6 tests) naming every fastmcp API the tool surface stands on. Mutation-checked both ways: removing the bound from one pin, and from all three, each fails a NAMED test with a specific message. 82 passed in the mcp_server chunk, 31 in version+requirement_gate, 3 in tests/test_packaging.py, ruff/black/mypy clean over CI's own paths. ONE CLAIM IN THIS ITEM'S DETAIL WAS WRONG and is corrected in the log: no test anywhere calls get_tools(); the seven files sit on list_tools(), which the research measured as SURVIVING 4.0.0. The research document was right; this queue item's paraphrase of it was not. The action stands on the remaining evidence.

queue.title: Full-surface e2e sweep against a fresh project on the 8011 Hub
queue.detail: This is the operator's 'run a e2e loop', and it is the highest-value item tonight. Invoke the e2e-loop skill. It has no mode flag -- the shape is set by how you answer its Step 1, 'Establish scope before looking at anything'. Set that scope to the FULL SURFACE, every feature area, not to a recent change. Then follow its steps 2-8 as written, including Step 8, Clean up. FIRST restart the drive Hub on 8011 from THIS branch's code and confirm no .py under hub/hub or src is newer than the process start time -- a stale build is the most expensive failure mode there is: cd hub && DATABASE_URL="sqlite+aiosqlite:///C:/Users/huida/.agentweave/hub/profiles/beta/agentweave.db" py -3.11 -m uvicorn hub.main:app --port 8011 --host 127.0.0.1   -- from hub/, from source, NEVER `agentweave --port` (its bundled migrations lag this checkout). 8011 is currently UP and healthy but was started from older code; restart it. Create a FRESH project. NEVER drive against proj-5e960453 (this repo) or proj-18e5d4e0. NEVER touch port 8000 -- that is the operator's real usage. 8010 is the other trial Hub; leave it alone. Every real agent turn binds claude-haiku-4-5 (standing operator directive, no budget gate). Never leave a job enabled. SPLIT THIS ACROSS ITERATIONS: one feature area per iteration, appending findings and committing as you go. One giant sweep that dies uncommitted loses the whole night. Every finding goes to scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md with a severity, a file:line, and a reproduction. A finding without a reproduction is a suspicion, and say so if that is all you have.

queue.title: F156 spec loop, round 1: explore and propose
queue.detail: F156 (severity B) is the cheapest unproposed finding and handoff 0102 ranked it next. 'integration-preview says will_merge: true for a task approval refuses outright.' Read its two sections in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md (search '## F156') -- the second records a deterministic reproduction and says the contrast lane is what turns it from a rough edge into a defect. hub/ui/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:66-79 moves with it. Write openspec/changes/<name>/ with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and the spec deltas. `openspec new change` refuses a name starting with a digit. `npx openspec validate --strict <name>` must pass, and it reads only a requirement's FIRST PHYSICAL LINE for the modal, so SHALL goes on line 1. Commit as `spec(round 1)`.

queue.title: F156 spec loop, round 2: independently re-derive against the code
queue.detail: Do NOT re-read round 1's reasoning and agree with it. Re-derive the argument from the actual code and fix the proposal where the code disagrees. This repository's dominant failure mode is a fix that passes its tests and cannot fire in production; the sharper variant is that an argument can be wrong while everything it argues about is right. State explicitly in the commit message what you changed, or that you changed nothing -- a round that finds nothing is a real outcome and hiding it makes the next one look cheaper than it is. Commit as `spec(round 2)`.

queue.detail: openspec-apply-change. Mutation-check anything you claim: delete the line the test exists for and watch a NAMED test fail; if nothing fails the test asserts over nothing. Then DRIVE it on 8011, restarted from the implementing code -- three rounds are not a substitute for driving it, and the first live drive has repeatedly found in one request what three rounds of reading missed. Reuse a harness in scripts/drive/ rather than writing a new one; scripts/drive/aw.py is what they all use. Record the result in FINDINGS.md, including anything the drive DISPROVES about the finding.
